title: GUTS - Journey of the Lone Wolf (Berserk analysis)
summary: A narrated literary portrait of Guts from Berserk as a traumatized lone wolf whose sword is his identity, until his defeat by Griffith forces him into a paradox and into the Band of the Hawk. Themes are self-discovery through peril, isolation versus belonging, and finding a name and an aim.
claims: For Guts the sword is his identity: killing is not only what he does but who he is
Self-discovery can happen through life-or-death struggle as validly as through contemplation; a man who cannot find himself in peril likely never will
The danger of finding yourself through combat is getting a taste for it and preferring to fight for your life rather than live it
A lifetime on the front lines thickened his body but could not erase the haunted gaze of someone whose past is his only future
Being spared by Griffith is the worst offense for someone prepared to die, and throws Guts into a paradox that redirects his bloodlust toward one man
Through the Hawks he learns that a fire's purpose is not only to burn but to comfort; joining a group gives him a name, and an aim gives him a self
